title: Strategic Ask Brief: Scenario Maps & Action Lanes for Q2 Roadmap Cadence
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Produce a concise executive-facing package that surfaces three Q2 investment scenarios for the inference platform, aligned asks for runway funding, and an action-lane playbook for follow-up. The package should allow the executive committee to: 1) choose a scenario, 2) see the concrete trade-offs (latency, unit cost, implementation effort, risk), and 3) approve a set of decision lanes that the product and engineering orgs will execute against over the quarter.

Context: Prior internal readouts focused on broad roadmap signals; executives requested a compact decision-first deliverable that frames multiple plausible cost/latency outcomes under different investment levels. This ticket consolidates inputs from runtime, infra, console, and finance to create a single-decision artifact.

Scope: Produce a 6-slide spotlight deck, a scenario map (3 scenarios: Optimize-for-Latency, Optimize-for-Cost, Balanced), a decision-lane checklist (actions, owners, gate criteria), a risk heatmap, and a 1-page roll-forward runbook for post-approval operationalization.
comments: 2026-02-07 - Aisha: Kickoff notes from cross-functional sync attached; asked runtime team for perf delta estimates and infra for cost delta by reservation size.

2026-02-10 - Runtime (Sonia): Provided benchmarking matrix for 3 model families across 64/128/256 token windows; highlighted KV cache improvements will shift Balanced scenario toward latency at low incremental cost.

2026-02-18 - Finance (Mark): Initial cost model shows >18% monthly cost delta between Optimize-for-Latency and Optimize-for-Cost at current usage profiles; recommended sensitivity table for 10/20/30% usage churn.
2026-02-25 - PM review (Liam): Draft slide set reviewed; requested clearer ask ladder (minimal ask, stretch ask) and explicit rollback criteria linked to quality regressions.
2026-03-02 - Design (Rina): Mockups for a compact heatmap and a one-line decision tile per scenario; suggested colorblind-safe palette and a microcopy refresh for executive consumption.

2026-03-05 - Eng lead (Diego): Raised a blocker: autoscaling tuning for Dedicated may require a small infra spike if we pursue Optimize-for-Latency; proposed a scoped canary to measure real-world impact before full commit.
2026-03-09 - PM owner (Liam): Incorporated canary plan as an action lane and moved the due date for runbook to 2026-03-20 to allow engineering validation.
2026-03-12 - Exec feedback (Sandra, CFO): Requested an explicit SLA delta table and a conservative spend cap for stretch asks; asked that a contingency lane be defined for 10% overrun.
decisions: Adopt three-scenario framing for exec presentation: Latency, Cost, Balanced.
Include a minimal ask (cover current ops + small optimizations) and a stretch ask (dedicated capacity + runtime ops for latency targets).
Require a 2-week canary for Dedicated autoscaling tuning before any full-scale capacity commit.
Add a contingency lane with a 10% spend cap and automatic rollback triggers tied to cost or correctness regressions.
risk_heatmap_summary: Primary risks: 1) Cost overrun if traffic volatility increases (mitigation: spend cap + throttled rollouts), 2) Quality regressions from aggressive quantization profiles (mitigation: eval sets + canary), 3) Autoscaling instability on Dedicated (mitigation: canary + runbook). Each risk is mapped to an action lane owner and gate criteria.
action_lanes: Lane A - Canary Autoscaling: Owner=ENG-SEV; Gate=stable throughput for 48h at 75th percentile load; Deliverable=runbook + metrics dashboard.
Lane B - Runtime Optimizations: Owner=Runtime Team; Gate=regression <0.5% on prompt-set; Deliverable=kernel selection config + quantization profile.
Lane C - Finance Guardrails: Owner=Finance PM; Gate=spend cap configured and alerting in place; Deliverable=automatic throttles + contingency funding approval.
Lane D - Exec Comms & Approval: Owner=Product Leadership; Gate=signoff on scenario and ask ladder; Deliverable=final spotlight deck and decision memo.
Lane E - Quality Monitoring: Owner=Applied ML; Gate=eval coverage for top-20 prompt sets; Deliverable=regression alerting + rollback playbook.

acceptance_criteria: Deck explains three scenarios in <6 slides and includes explicit ask ladder (minimal vs stretch).
Scenario cost tables validated by Finance and Ops (variance <8% to model).
Runbook for canary exists and has been executed for at least 48h with metrics captured.
Exec signoff or clear follow-up action lane accepted by Product Leadership.
